verses.text: Early that morning, the chief priests met with the elders, legal teachers, and the whole council. They tied Jesus up, took him away, and handed him over to Pilate.
Pilate asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus answered, “That’s what you say.”
The chief priests brought many accusations against him.
Pilate questioned him again: “Aren’t you going to answer? Look at how many charges they’re bringing against you!”
But Jesus gave no further answer, and Pilate was amazed.
At the festival, Pilate usually released one prisoner—the one the people asked for.
There was a man called Barabbas, locked up with fellow rebels who had committed murder during an uprising.
The crowd came forward, shouting and asking Pilate to do what he usually did for them.
Pilate asked them, “Do you want me to release the King of the Jews?”
He knew the chief priests had handed Jesus over because they were jealous.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to get Pilate to release Barabbas instead.
Pilate asked them again, “Then what should I do with the man you call the King of the Jews?”
They shouted back, “Crucify him!”
Pilate said, “Why? What has he done wrong?” But they shouted even louder, “Crucify him!”
Pilate wanted to satisfy the crowd, so he released Barabbas. After having Jesus whipped, he handed him over to be crucified.
The soldiers took Jesus into the courtyard—the Praetorium—and called together the whole cohort.
They dressed him in purple, twisted thorn branches into a crown, and placed it on him.
Then they started saluting him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They hit his head with a reed, spat on him, and knelt down as if honoring him.
After mocking him, they took off the purple robe and put his own clothes back on him. Then they led him out to crucify him.
A man named Simon of Cyrene, Alexander and Rufus’s father, was coming in from the countryside. They forced him to carry Jesus’ cross.
They brought Jesus to Golgotha, a name that means “Place of a Skull.”
They offered him wine mixed with myrrh, but he wouldn’t drink it.
They crucified him and divided his clothes among themselves, throwing lots to decide who got what.
It was nine in the morning when they crucified him.
The charge against him was written above him: “THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
They crucified two robbers with him, one on his right and one on his left.
This fulfilled the Scripture that says, “He was counted among lawbreakers.”
People passing by insulted him and shook their heads: “Hey! You said you’d destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days.
“Save yourself and come down from the cross!”
The chief priests and legal teachers were mocking him too, saying to each other, “He saved others, but he can’t save himself.
“Let the Christ, Israel’s King, come down from the cross now, so we can see and believe!” Even the people crucified beside him insulted him.
At noon, darkness covered the whole land until three in the afternoon.
At three, Jesus cried out loudly, “Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?” That means, “My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?”
Some people standing nearby heard him and said, “Look, he’s calling Elijah.”
One person ran, filled a sponge with vinegar, put it on a reed, and offered it to Jesus to drink. He said, “Let’s see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”
Jesus cried out loudly and breathed his last.
The temple curtain ripped in two, from top to bottom.
The centurion standing opposite Jesus saw how he cried out and died. He said, “This man really was the Son of God!”
Some women were watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and Joses, and Salome.
They had followed Jesus and cared for him when he was in Galilee. Many other women had also come with him to Jerusalem.
By evening, since it was Preparation Day—the day before the Sabbath—
Joseph of Arimathaea arrived. He was a respected council member who was also waiting for God’s Kingdom. He boldly went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body.
Pilate was surprised Jesus had already died. He called the centurion over and asked whether Jesus had been dead for a while.
After getting confirmation from the centurion, Pilate gave the body to Joseph.
Joseph bought a linen cloth, took Jesus down, wrapped him in it, and laid him in a tomb cut into rock. Then he rolled a stone across the tomb’s entrance.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where Jesus was laid.
